title: Cohort Warmup Playlist & Rollback Cheat (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for a low-risk feature/model flip. This is a lightweight, highly actionable playlist I carry when I own a quiet window rollout. Keep terse: what to do, when, and the exact rollback trigger + commands.

High-level objective:
- Introduce model variant V2 to production with minimal customer impact, validate quality signals and cache behavior, then widen if stable. Avoid full pin unless regressions justify it.

Cohort sequence (playlist style):
1) Shadow probe (0% routing) — 30m
   - Send mirrored requests to V2, observe token-level outputs and latency. No KV warming. Use small sample clients (10-20 tenants).
2) Edge-bucket warmup (1% traffic) — 45m
   - Route 1% of traffic from an edge bucket (non-critical tenants). Purpose: exercise cold-starts, early batch shapes. Start with sample size ~500 requests.
3) Priming wave (5% traffic) — 1h
   - Inject curated priming set: synthetic prompts that exercise long-context behavior and typical user flows. Fill KV cache by sending prefix requests via the priming runner. Monitor KV hit rate and token cost.
4) Gradual fade-in (15% -> 40%) — incremental 15% steps every 30–60m
   - Observe latency P50/P90/P99, error spike windows, and quality regression metrics (QA pass rate on eval set).
5) Anchor cohorts (60% then steady) — only if all metrics green for 3h
   - Move majority traffic, keep a permanent 10% holdout cohort as final safety.

Priming actions (explicit):
- KV cache priming: run the priming runner (tools/priming/prime.sh) with seed prompts for top-100 prefixes. Budget: 25k tokens per region.
- Prefix spoofing: send lightweight echo prompts to encourage LRU retention for common client tokens (safe for privacy; avoid real PII).
- Shadow reranker checks: send outputs to reranker pipeline and diff score distributions.

Instrumentation & metrics to watch (live dashboards):
- Latency: p50/p90/p99 per region and per model variant
- Errors: 5xx, timeouts, IO errors, client-aborted requests
- Output divergence: % of responses flagged as low-confidence vs baseline (redwood-eval/quickset)
- Token cost delta: per-request token consumption + cache-hit ratio
- KV-cache hit rate: warm cache percent within first 100 tokens
- Tracing: end-to-end request latency, queueing time, batch sizes

Rollout safety thresholds (auto/hand triggers):
- Immediate rollback (auto): p99 latency > baseline + 400ms for two consecutive 5m windows OR error rate increase > 3x baseline over 10m
- Manual review threshold: QA pass delta drops > 2.5 percentage points vs baseline in 30m window
- Cost guardrail: per-token cost delta > 40% sustained over 1h

Manual rollback checklist (fast path):
1) Issue: Execute routing revert on routing API: curl -X POST $ROUTE_API/revert -d '{"route":"/gen","variant":"stable"}' (team-safe token required).
2) Re-pin: If client pin needed: update config via console -> tenant -> overrides -> set model=stable + pin_reason="rollback-<timestamp>".
3) Invalidate warm caches where necessary: run tools/cache/invalidate --variant=v2 --regions=us-west,eu
4) Notify: #release-alerts + affected owners, include short changelog and rollback reason.
5) Postmortem stub: create JIRA RL-xxxxx, add initial hypotheses.

Automation hooks & quick commands:
- Reweight route (non-destructive): /admin/reweight?path=/gen&variant=v2&pct=15
- Canary resample: tools/canary/resample --tenants-list=lists/edge-buckets/edge-01 --pct=1
- Live eval runner: tools/eval/run --suite=smoke-priming --model=v2 --window=30m

Open questions / guardrails I still want answered before next quiet window:
- How to safely prime KV cache for multi-tenant embedding churn without exposing cross-tenant tokens? (draft idea: tenant-local prefix lists + TTL policy)
- Should SDK include an explicit client-side holdout toggle so we can do per-client gradual enablement instead of purely server-side routing? Pros/cons?
- Need a synthetic workload generator that matches our real heavy tail (queueing profile). Current priming set feels too uniform.

TODOS (mine / short):
- [ ] Finalize priming prompt list (top 120 prefixes) — ask Jin for latest telemetry dump
- [ ] Add a quick revert runbook snippet to /playbooks/rollback-quick.md (one-liner commands)
- [ ] Run a rehearsal in staging with same batch sizes tomorrow 09:30 PT

Notes / personal heuristics:
- Prefer conservative heat for first 3 hours; many regressions surface after 30–90m when caches misalign.
- Keep a permanent 5–10% cold holdout group for final validation; catches subtle regressions.
- If KV cache hit rate is low despite priming, suspect mismatch in prefix tokenization or batch composition — check tokenization service and batching window.

End of scratch. If I return to this doc, will add CLI examples and link to the exact priming runner. For now: playbook in pocket.
